who: Susan M. Hill, historian of Haudenosaunee land tenure at Western University before 2017; PhD in Native Studies, Trent University.

evidence.says: The September 2017 university profile identifies Hill as formerly associate professor of history and director of First Nations Studies at Western, with a PhD in Native Studies from Trent.
Lists her publications under Susan M. Hill, including The Clay We Are Made Of: Haudenosaunee Land Tenure on the Grand River (2017), and her Trent PhD.
The authority record identifies Susan M. Hill through the title page of The Clay We Are Made Of (2017).

notes: The Susan M. Hill candidate matches the Western affiliation, Trent doctorate and research field. She moved to Toronto in 2017, shortly before the listed dissertation completion.

who: James H. Jones, historian of medicine who taught at the University of Houston.

evidence.says: The author affiliation identifies James H. Jones as a historian who taught at the University of Houston and the University of Arkansas.
The candidate item identifies James Rees Jones and lists the University of East Anglia as his employer.
James Rees Jones specialized in seventeenth-century England and held posts at Newcastle and the University of East Anglia.

notes: The candidate is James Rees Jones, a different historian from Houston medical historian James H. Jones.

who: Emory Leland Kemp, historian of technology and civil engineering professor at West Virginia University, 1962–2003.

evidence.says: The university finding aid identifies Emory Leland Kemp and records his teaching of civil engineering, historic preservation and the history of technology at WVU from 1962 to 2003.
The candidate authority identifies Eric Waldram Kemp, author of Canonization and Authority in the Western Church and a fellow of Exeter College, Oxford.

notes: Emory Leland Kemp at WVU and candidate Eric Waldram Kemp at Oxford are different people.

who: E. Patricia Tsurumi, historian of Japan at the University of Victoria, which she joined in 1972.

evidence.says: The dissertation title page names Dr. E. P. Tsurumi of the History Department as supervisor of Michiko Midge Ayukawa’s Creating and Recreating Community: Hiroshima and Canada 1891–1941.
UVic identifies E. Patricia Tsurumi as its historian of Japan, notes her arrival in 1972, and explicitly discusses her encouragement of Midge Ayukawa’s doctoral research.
The authority identifies E. Patricia Tsurumi, cites The Other Japan (1987), and records a Harvard PhD in Japanese history in 1971.

notes: Direct dissertation supervision evidence confirms the identity. The repository thesis is dated 1996, while the supplied AHA entry gives 1997.

who: Martin Mulsow, historian of early modern intellectual culture; Rutgers professor from 2005, then Erfurt from July 2008; PhD Munich 1991.

evidence.says: His institutional CV records a 1991 philosophy doctorate at Munich, a Rutgers history professorship in 2005, and the Erfurt appointment beginning July 2008; research includes radical Enlightenment.
The candidate authority cites the Erfurt faculty CV and identifies the same Munich philosophy doctorate (1991) and Erfurt professorship from 2008.

notes: The authority and institutional CV identify the same scholar; the Rutgers appointment overlaps Groetsch’s 2008 dissertation and matches its Enlightenment field.

who: Tom F. Peters, professor of art, architecture and history at Lehigh University; doctorate ETH Zurich 1977.

evidence.says: The 2003–04 catalogue lists Tom F. Peters in the history faculty and as professor of art, architecture and history, with an ETH Zurich doctorate (1977); he teaches building-construction history.
The candidate authority identifies Thomas J. Peters, management consultant and business-management author, through The Secrets of Excellence and A Passion for Excellence.

notes: Lehigh construction historian Tom F. Peters is different from management writer Thomas J. Peters.

who: Anthony J. Podlecki, scholar of ancient Greek history and literature at Penn State, 1966–1975; PhD Toronto 1963.

evidence.says: The Database of Classical Scholars records his Toronto PhD (1963) and service as professor and head of classics at Penn State, 1966–1975.
Podlecki’s university newsletter account says he held posts at Northwestern and Penn State before joining UBC in 1975; his research covers archaic and classical Greek history and literature.
The candidate authority identifies Anthony J. Podlecki through The Early Greek Poets and Their Times (1984) and Euripides’ Medea (1991).

notes: The candidate’s field and Penn State appointment in 1973 match the supervisor and dissertation.

who: William L. Sherman, historian of colonial Mexico and Central America at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln; PhD New Mexico 1967.

evidence.says: The Spanish archival authority identifies William L. Sherman as a Nebraska–Lincoln history professor specializing in colonial Mexico and Central America, with a University of New Mexico doctorate in 1967.
The AHA programme lists William L. Sherman, University of Nebraska, Lincoln, presenting on sixteenth-century Central America.
The candidate authority identifies William L. Sherman through his work Victoriano Huerta (1960).

notes: The William L. Sherman candidate matches the university and colonial Latin American field of Vincent’s dissertation.
